chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali and Abu Qatadah Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Hafth al-Qummi, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about the days of Al-Adha (Qurbani), how many days are they in Mina? He said, 'Four days.' And I asked him about Al-Adha outside of Mina, he said, 'Three days.' I said, 'What do you say about a traveler who arrived after Al-Adha by two days? Is it permissible for him to offer the sacrifice on the third day?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: The ritual animal sacrifice offered during Eid al-Adha
key_terms.الْيَوْمِ الثَّالِثِ: The third day of Dhu al-Hijjah
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a location near Mecca where sacrifices are traditionally offered during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible days for offering the Eid al-Adha sacrifice in Mina compared to other places, and is it valid for late-arriving travelers?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the temporal boundaries of the Udhiyah, distinguishing the four-day period in Mina from the three-day window elsewhere, reflecting the jurisprudential nuance between the Eid al-Adha days and the days of Tashriq. It further establishes a practical concession (rukhsah) for travelers, ensuring the ritual's accessibility despite logistical delays, a principle often cited in Shia fiqh regarding the flexibility of sacrificial timing.
